nik: Heads-up: sampleapp started throwing a flurry of RejectedExecutionException errors after the new retry/circuit-breaker changes. App becomes very slow then a bunch of requests fail fast.

tara: Logs? stacktrace?

nik: ```
java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException: Task java.util.concurrent.FutureTask@6a2b0 rejected from java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor@1f3b4[Running, pool size = 5, active threads = 5, queued tasks = 0, completed tasks = 120]
 at java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor.reject(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:...)
 at java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor.execute(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:...)
 at okhttp3.internal.concurrent.TaskRunner.execute(TaskRunner.kt:...)
```

leo: Interesting. The ThreadPoolExecutor there looks like OkHttp's TaskRunner backed pool. Are we spawning blocking refreshes that consume the pool?

nik: We traced it: when token expires, the Authenticator and an internal retry interceptor both try to refresh simultaneously. Each call ends up invoking authClient.refreshSync() which uses the library client (shared OkHttp) synchronously. Under heavy concurrency those refreshes saturate the TaskRunner pool and subsequent enqueued tasks are rejected.

aina: Can you paste the interceptor and authenticator snippets?

nik: Sure (simplified):
```kotlin
class RetryInterceptor : Interceptor {
  override fun intercept(chain: Interceptor.Chain): Response {
    val resp = chain.proceed(chain.request())
    if (shouldRetry(resp)) {
      // sync refresh and retry
      val tok = authClient.refreshSync()
      val newReq = chain.request().newBuilder().header("Authorization", "Bearer $tok").build()
      return chain.proceed(newReq)
    }
    return resp
  }
}

class TokenAuthenticator : Authenticator {
  override fun authenticate(route: Route?, response: Response): Request? {
    val tok = authClient.refreshSync() // uses same client
    return response.request.newBuilder().header("Authorization", "Bearer $tok").build()
  }
}
```

tara: Double refresh + shared client = classic self-deadlock / pool exhaustion. Also retry interceptor calling chain.proceed after doing blocking work can be unsafe since it's on the OkHttp worker thread.

leo: On Android, this looked like random RejectedExecutionException (not main-thread) but result is the same: requests fail under burst. We should recommend using a non-blocking token provider or a dedicated client for refresh path.

nik: I prototyped a fix: a TokenProvider singleton that returns current token immediately (volatile cached string) and, if stale, triggers a background refresh using a single-threaded executor that uses a dedicated OkHttpClient (separate dispatcher and connection pool). Then both Authenticator and Interceptor consult the provider instead of calling authClient directly.

aina: Nice. Any race where two refreshes still get triggered concurrently?

nik: The provider uses a compare-and-set backed refreshInFlight flag (AtomicBoolean) so only one background refresh runs. Others keep using the cached token or wait for a short timeout.

tara: Please add an example to sampleapp and a comment block explaining why sharing the same client for token refresh is risky. Also add a unit test that simulates many concurrent requests with forced expiry.

nik: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/sampleapp/pull/952 (WIP) with the TokenProvider and integration test.

ci-bot: Created issue #4380: "threadpool exhaustion from sync auth refresh + retry interceptor" - https://git.internal/redwood/issues/4380 :gear:

leo: For SDK guidance, we should add a short note in the okhttp/retrofit guide:
  - Don't do blocking refreshes on the same OkHttp client from Authenticator/Interceptor.
  - Prefer token provider pattern or dedicated refresh client.
  - If you must refresh synchronously, use a client with its own Dispatcher (smaller pool) and connection pool to avoid starving the main pool.

aina: Also call out that chain.proceed should not be used after doing blocking network IO from interceptor threads; switch to async patterns or move logic to a higher layer where possible.

tara: I'll slot a small change into the onboarding checklist and add a note in the migration doc for v0.13.0.

nik: Leaving a short repro recipe in the PR and adding the logs plus the failing test. Will iterate on feedback. Thanks all.
